Questions

Questions about the teaching

Understanding the Creator and the game.

We are the Creator. We created this game of experiences and entered it. Having designed it before entering, we cannot change its design from inside the game.

What is the central statement?

We are the Creator. We created this game of experiences and entered it. Having designed it before entering, we cannot change its design from inside the game. Every lesson and exercise on this site develops this spiritual philosophy of Uday Kumar.

Who does “we are the Creator” refer to?

It refers to the one shared source, God or Shakti, appearing through different lives and roles. In this philosophy, everyone belongs to that identity. It does not mean that one personality is superior to others or can control the game from outside.

Why did the Creator enter the game?

In Uday’s account, the one Creator was alone and made this existence for experiences. We encounter its changing scenes through many lives and roles. Remembering that source while experiencing the game is the central aim of the teaching.

If the game cannot be changed, why make an effort?

The total design cannot be rewritten from inside, in this philosophy. Effort, decisions, learning, remembrance, and repair are themselves parts of its unfolding. We experience them within the game and do not know the next scene in advance. Participating thoughtfully does not place us outside the design.

How is understanding different from repeating a belief?

The exercises invite you to examine what the teaching means in a particular scene: which role has absorbed you, what outcome you demand, and what remembering the shared Creator changes. Reciting the statement alone does not establish understanding. You can question it, and an experience of calm does not independently prove its account of creation.

How do the movie and lotus explain emotions?

The movie illustrates becoming absorbed and then remembering the wider context. The lotus is Uday’s image of living within the pond of life so lightly that it seems unclear whether its water touches us. Both point to remembrance of the Creator within the already-designed game while emotions are experienced. They do not require emotional numbness or an immediate disappearance of feelings.

Why is responsibility described as arising naturally?

Within the teaching, seeing ourselves and others as the same Creator changes the meaning of a relationship. Care is understood to arise from that recognition. The exercises therefore return to who we are and how we experience the game, rather than making responsibility a separate command. Effects in an individual’s life still need honest examination.

How do possessions and relationships fit the teaching?

Gold, diamonds, money, and status are small parts of creation in Uday’s explanation. They cannot enlarge the Creator’s identity. Remembering the same Creator in another person can restore the importance of a relationship when a possession dominates attention. Practical needs and agreements still belong to the game; the teaching does not ask us to ignore them.

Does seeing the same Creator mean accepting harm?

No. Protecting a life, setting a boundary, and repairing harm also concern the shared creation. These actions occur within the game. Creator-awareness does not erase consent or consequences, and does not require anyone to remain in danger.

What if the mind does not become silent?

The teaching connects a quieter mind with releasing the role’s demand to control the whole game. Begin with one ordinary scene and examine that demand gently. Silence cannot be forced by repeating “I am the Creator.” If reflection becomes uncomfortable or overwhelming, stop and return to ordinary activity or suitable support.

Does this prove we created the universe or guarantee success?

No. These pages explain Uday’s spiritual philosophy. Analogies, scriptural interpretations, and reflections can help examine it, but do not independently prove a predetermined universe. Remembering the Creator is the intended focus; particular emotional, financial, or health outcomes are not guaranteed.

Where should I begin?

Read the root statement, including the part about being unable to rewrite the game from inside. Then take one small event through the five-minute practice. Examine how remembering the Creator relates to the role, emotion, and response within that scene, and record what changed or did not change.
